coverage.boundaryAssessment: The eight saved transitions separate the microscopic model, latent heat, critical-temperature comparison, pressure trend, constrained freezing and three prose worked examples without breaking an example's derivation. blocks.substance: Pure crystalline substance, specified pressure, approximate two-phase equilibrium and absence of other phase/chemical changes retained. Impurities, nucleation and heating/cooling dependence preserved; textbook ice0C, mercury-39C and tin232C remain approximate at standard atmospheric pressure. Mercury comparison-only/no handling retained.

Fixed-pressure equilibrium melting needs transferred heat. Already equilibrated unchanged constraints/no net heat or other energy exchange are not confused with isolation alone. Internal adjustment, crystal-formation conditions, equal equilibrium phase temperatures and possible supercooling remain distinct.

Atoms/ions/molecules and simple classical thermal-motion model retained. English does not make a universal kinetic/potential partition. Approximately constant-temperature melting, simplified microscopic explanation, enthalpy/internal energy and external work remain separate; contraction of ice and inability to infer latent heat from volume alone retained.

Specific latent heat of fusion is explicitly phase-change heat per unit mass, usual J/kg, at specified pressure and melting temperature; complete same-temperature melting excludes preheating and later liquid heating. The standard English term is faithful to the Chinese textbook term, not a new quantity.

Reversed initial/final states at the same pressure preserve equal heat magnitudes/opposite signs. Cloud freezing/deposition is not guaranteed ground warming. Retained3.4e5J/kg=80cal/g is expressly rounded, not exact. Spring rapid-melting counterfactual is not an actual seconds/minutes prediction; mass, initial temperature and incoming heat still govern melting.

Massm, already-at-melting-temperature, specified-pressure and complete same-temperature melting conditions plus separate pre/post-heating are all faithful. The first sentence's dangling 'is:' is interrupted by two qualifier sentences before the formula, creating the required local flow repair EN54-F1.
Q_melt=lambda m and equation6-7 retained; English subscript names the same melting heat, with no changed sign, mass or coefficient.
Heat entering the substance positive, released crystallization heat negative, positive release magnitude, and exclusion of cooling before/after phase change retained.
Q_cryst=-lambda m and equation6-8 preserve the declared signed-heat convention.

Vaporization/fusion comparison stays far below liquid-gas critical temperature and nonuniversal. Approximate water valuesL2.26e6J/kg at100C andlambda3.4e5J/kg at0C are explicitly different-temperature phase changes. No crystal long-range order or quantitative structural similarity is assigned to liquid; near-critical limits remain.

Usual solid/liquid phases and limited pressure range qualify expansion/raised equilibrium melting point. Smaller-volume phase, volume difference and phase heat explanation retained without universal potential-energy claim. Boiling is a separate liquid-gas equilibrium.

Ordinary ice/bismuth volume decrease and same-mass density increase preserved. Floating ice and pressure-lowered melting are not extended to every high-pressure phase. Open structure, order/disorder limits and positive latent heat despite contraction remain.

Ordinary freezing expansion, insufficient space and constrained-container load can cause rupture. Iron sphere/glass bottle remain conceptual examples; no sealed-freezing/bursting procedure supplied. Flying-fragment hazard, do-not-attempt instruction and structure/space/process/pressure dependence retained.
Crack-water forces and repeated freeze-thaw weathering are conditional on water content, crack structure and temperature change, not inevitable fracture of every cold rock.
Worked-examples heading stays prose; no practice task is generated.
BrassD0.8mm, unloadedL3.6m, axialF25N and extension2mm preserved. Uniform specimen, constant cross section, small-strain linear elasticity and neglect of clamping deformation retained.
Hooke relation and E=sigma/absolute strain retained. The problem length symbol and subsequent initial-length symbol explicitly denote the same unloaded length; no identity substitution is hidden.
Uniform axial stressF/S and strain|Delta l|/l0 use initial gauge length and unloaded area; small-strain area change neglected.
E=F l0/(S|Delta l|) remains the approved formula.
Circular area piD^2/4 and E=4F l0/(piD^2|Delta l|) retained with consistent-length-unit instruction.
Rounded textbookE9e10N/m^2 preserved as this specimen/model result, not a universal brass constant at every state/temperature. D016 calculation reused without solving again.

Example2 ice0.4kg at0C, aluminum container75C and final50C, unknown containerm1 andc1=880J/(kg degree) retained. Evaporation/external heat/other initial heat capacities excluded; ordinary-pressure phase change, constant specific-heat ranges and no hot-container handling retained.
